title: For an engineering leader
reader: a CTO or engineering leader whose teams already use coding agents
judges: Does "brakes let you go faster" fit what is known about delivery performance, and what would I copy?
why_you: You run engineering where agents already ship code. If the speed in these chapters is only activity, or the gates are ones your teams already have under another name, you will see it first.

ask.by_note: an example date: nothing has been sent

gets: your name in the acknowledgements, if you want it there
the first edition when it ships
a reply to every comment, and a page showing what your comments changed

chapters.why: the machine: wakes, the gate and releases, every hour
brakes under deadline: what held, what bent, and what stopped the team

chapters_note: A proposal by developer@, from the reviewers study's themes for this reader; which length every page aims at is the editor's question.

questions.q: What is the machine, in one sentence, as you would explain it to your team?
Does the record show speed, or only activity? What would show you the difference?
Which practice you already run (change approval, branch protection, release gates) is this closest to, and where does it differ?
What would break first if you ran it with your own teams?
Which failure here matters most to you, and is it told fairly?
Was the brake that fired the right one? What should have fired instead?
Does the chapter show what the team should have done, or only what it did?
What would you test before a deadline like this one?

short_note: the one chapter to read when short of time: a proposal by developer@ from synthetic@'s runs, for the editor to keep or change
